CISO.sign_convention: Sources are drawn positive and sinks negative. All arrays in dispatch_results and dispatch_model are non-negative magnitudes except net_imports_mw, which is signed: positive = import (a source, series `imports`), negative = export (a sink, series `exports`, drawn below zero as its magnitude). fixed_other_mw is clamped at zero (never a sink). Battery charging and curtailment are sinks. The LP balance uses net_imports_mw with its sign.

constraints: balance[t]: sum_c g[c,t] - curtS[t] - curtW[t] + dis[t] - ch[t] + uns[t] = Dnet[t] - Savail[t] - Wavail[t]; Dnet = demand*demand_scale + heat_shock - imports - fixed_other
soc[t] - soc[t-1] - eta*ch[t] + dis[t]/eta = 0 with soc[-1] = soc0*E, eta = sqrt(round_trip_eff)
ramp: |g[c,t] - g[c,t-1]| <= ramp_frac*capacity for t = 1..23 (two rows each)

bounds: min(pmin*cap, cap*a) <= g <= cap*a (a = 1 - outage_pct/100 for the outaged class, else 1), 0 <= curt <= availability, 0 <= ch,dis <= battery_power_mw, soc_min*E <= soc <= E with E = battery_power_mw * battery_hours, soc[23] >= soc0*E, uns >= 0
formulation.controls_note: Control ids are the keys of every params object. battery energy = battery_power_mw * battery_hours. demand scale = 1 + demand_growth_pct/100. outage removes outage_pct percent of one class's capacity (its minimum output stays, capped at the remaining capacity, so an outage never lowers cost); 'none' disables it.
formulation.heat_shock: heat_shock[h] = b_cool[h] * (max(T[h] + heat_wave_c - Tc, 0) - max(T[h] - Tc, 0)) from weather_relation.json
formulation.objective: min sum_t [ sum_c cost[c]*g[c,t] + wear*dis[t] + VOLL*uns[t] ]; reported cost = solver objective; the breakdown by class sums to it
formulation.price_definition: price_usd_mwh[t] = row dual of balance[t] = d(objective_usd)/d(Dnet[t]): USD per extra MWh of demand in hour t. Positive when more demand raises cost; equals the marginal cost of the marginal class, VOLL (1000) when load is shed, about 0 in curtailment hours. In HiGHS' sign convention for a minimisation problem. Unique only when the LP is non-degenerate at that hour (see price_comparable in the test vectors).
row_order: soc rows t = 0..23 (row 0 has right-hand side soc0*E)
hydro energy row (if a hydro class exists)
for each dispatchable class c in order, for t = 1..23: ramp-up row (g[c,t]-g[c,t-1] <= R) then ramp-down row (g[c,t-1]-g[c,t] <= R)
formulation.solver: HiGHS via highspy 1.15.1 (HiGHS 1.15.1), simplex, presolve on, 1 thread, in Python; the browser build declares highs@1.15.3 (HiGHS-wasm), not run in this repo
formulation.summary: Single-node 24-hour least-cost dispatch. Minimise fuel/VOM cost + battery wear + value-of-lost-load penalty subject to hourly energy balance, battery state of charge, hydro daily energy, ramp limits and capacity bounds.
variable_order: g: index c*24 + t, classes in the order of `classes` filtered to kind=dispatchable
variables: g[c,t] dispatchable class output MW (c in dispatchable classes, t = 0..23)
curtS[t], curtW[t] curtailed solar and wind MW (used = availability*renewables_scale - curtailment)
ch[t], dis[t] battery charge and discharge MW
soc[t] battery energy MWh at the END of hour t (t = 0..23; the start-of-day SoC is the constant soc0)
